brief:
Israel is heading to the polls for the first time since the 7 October attacks, with national security dominating campaign messaging, The Guardian reported. The election reflects heightened focus on defense and military response to the attacks that triggered the conflict.

Campaign rhetoric has shifted decisively toward security-focused platforms as voters weigh competing approaches to national defense. Candidates are stressing military preparedness and defense policy as central issues in the race.
dek: Israel is heading to the polls for the first time since the 7 October attacks and concerns about national security are dominating the campaign.
title: Security concerns shape Israeli election after October 7 attacks
